scoutingParagraphs: Hiroike is a 22-year-old Keio University right-hander entering through the international amateur route, rather than as an established NPB professional or teenage J15 signing. Sanspo reported an agreement in principle with the Yankees on November 22, earlier than the initial November 23 summary. Completion and bonus remain unconfirmed; a November 29 trip for a physical was reported.

His final Tokyo Big6 season produced 51 strikeouts in 44 innings with a 2.66 ERA. The fall included five starts and 32 strikeouts against 104 batters (30.8%). That is an encouraging starter audition, but only 25 fall innings: command, recovery and effectiveness deeper into games remain open questions.

In his November 5 Keio Sports Press interview, Hiroike described redesigning his slider and evaluating pitch movement and missed bats. He reported about 15 cm more horizontal and vertical movement, with a roughly 5–6% increase in his whiff-rate measure; the denominator and percent-versus-percentage-point interpretation cannot be independently checked. He also cited a 148.8 km/h (92.5 mph) fall fastball average. These are player-reported tracking summaries, not publicly audited measurements.

Pipeline view: the improving fastball/slider combination and documented collegiate bat-missing earn a meaningful place on this board. His age, limited workload, prolonged forearm-injury recovery and unresolved third pitch leave substantial relief and injury risk. The Yankees destination is development context, not an automatic valuation premium.

ranking.basis: Independent cross-period editorial dynasty placement; not an industry rank or eligibility confirmation
ranking.rationale: Placed #24, just ahead of Tatsuya Nogami, on stronger verified hardball collegiate competition and final-season strikeout evidence. Nogami is younger with a larger listed frame and a confirmed signing; Hiroike’s age, injury history and pending physical keep the gap small. Remains well below Shoki Oda and the premium bats: a short fall starter sample does not establish starter durability.

performanceEvidence.label: Collegiate league record
performanceEvidence.detail: Career: 29 G, 80⅔ IP, 4–3, 3.12 ERA, 82 K. 2026 spring: 6 G, 19 IP, 19 K, 2.37 ERA; fall: 6 G, 25 IP, 32 K, 2.88 ERA. Combined: 12 G, 44 IP, 51 K, 13 ER, 2.66 ERA, 10.43 K/9. Combined rates are calculated from official counts; league games only.

performanceEvidence.label: Fall 2026 strikeouts and baserunners
performanceEvidence.detail: 5 starts; 104 batters faced; 17 hits, 2 HR and 11 walks plus hit batters. K% 30.8%; BB+HBP% 10.6%; K/9 11.52; H/9 6.12; HR/9 0.72. Walks and HBP are combined in the retrieved table, so 10.6% is not a conventional BB%. Opponent context matters: 10 of the 32 strikeouts came against Tokyo.

performanceEvidence.label: Velocity context
performanceEvidence.detail: Game peak: 154 km/h (95.7 mph). Player-reported fall average: 148.8 km/h (92.5 mph). Advertised 156 km/h (96.9 mph) maximum is a bullpen reading. No verified full-season game velocity distribution; the supplied 87–91 mph spring range is not published as established sitting velocity.

performanceEvidence.label: Injury history
performanceEvidence.detail: Hiroike described neck symptoms, then a forearm muscle injury in spring 2025 and a prolonged recovery. He made no fall 2025 league appearances and described shoulder/elbow discomfort during spring 2026. Reported summer improvement is not proof of present health.

developmentCheckpoint.name: Kosei Hiroike
developmentCheckpoint.topic: Healthy starter workload and usable third pitch
developmentCheckpoint.question: Can Hiroike sustain game velocity, strikes and slider quality through consecutive professional starts while developing a third pitch?
developmentCheckpoint.baseline: 2026 league workload: 44 IP / 51 K; fall 25 IP over five starts and one relief outing. Prior forearm injury and prolonged recovery remain relevant; 96.9 mph was a bullpen peak.
developmentCheckpoint.positive: Physical and contract are confirmed; multiple dated outings show stable game velocity, recovery between starts, competitive strike location and a third offering that works against opposite-handed hitters.
developmentCheckpoint.concern: Recurring arm symptoms, declining velocity or ineffective secondary separation persist across outings; walks plus hit batters and inefficient counts undermine starter workload.
developmentCheckpoint.window: Check contract/physical after the reported November 29 travel, then first assignment. Review several full professional outings and recovery cycles; do not promote from a single radar reading.
developmentCheckpoint.evidence: Final official collegiate records and first-person development reports support an initial starter audition. These are future checkpoints, not progress already achieved.
